text:
jin: Heads up — noticed the PR that updates the model_support table has an inconsistent field name for the quantized variants. The catalog CSV uses `quant_profile` but the model card examples and SDK snippets use `quantization_profile`. This is causing failing tests in the SDK integration tests.

sara: oh no. which PR? link?

jin: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/987 (the one that added the Petra-Lite entry). Failing test log: 
```
AssertionError: missing field 'quantization_profile' in model_card.examples.snippet
Expected keys: name, family, quantization_profile, seq_limit
Found: name, family, quant_profile, seq_limit
```

dan: thanks for catching. Sounds like a quick rename but we should add a migration note so SDK2 consumers don't break.

natalie: agreed. small tasks: 1) update CSV -> `quantization_profile` 2) patch model card snippet to match 3) add a compatibility note in the model catalog doc 4) add a unit test for both key names for a transitional release. I can take 1 and 2.

jin: amazing, can you also drop a short example snippet that shows both legacy and new keys so the SDK can accept both for 1 release?

alex: SDK side: we already added a lenient parser in sdk-python that looks for `quant_profile` as fallback, but the docs need to reflect timeline. I'll open a tiny PR to the SDK tests to assert both keys are accepted for one major.

sara: for the model card snippet, we should also clarify the effect on `seq_limit` for Petra-Lite (it's lower because of the reduced KV cache). People were using Petra-Lite for long-context demos and hitting truncation.

jin: right — bench numbers in the PR claim 8k seq, but on small GPU it's closer to 4k when quantized. We should correct the Limits section and add a short paragraph explaining quantized long-context tradeoffs.

natalie: drafting patch now. Proposed text for the Limits note: 
> Note: Petra-Lite's quantized variants reduce available KV cache; recommend limiting sequence length to 4096 for quantized runs on small GPUs. For higher seq needs, use non-quantized or a variant with extended KV.

dan: good. Add a link to the Optimize guide (https://docs.redwood.ai/optimize/quantization) and maybe a short example command for CI benchmarking.

natalie: adding this: 
```
# quick local perf sample (benchmark harness)
python bench.py --model petra-lite-quant --seq 4096 --batch 1
```

alex: SDK PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk/pull/222 — tests updated to accept fallback key and log a deprecation warning.

jin: can we include a one-line deprecation blurb in the model catalog top-level changelog? That helps customers scanning release notes.

sara: I'll add: "Deprecated field `quant_profile` will be accepted for one release; please migrate to `quantization_profile`. See migration notes on the Petra-Lite model card."

docs-bot: reminder: when you update the model card please increment the card version in the frontmatter and add an entry to models/CHANGELOG.md or the PR will fail lint.

natalie: thanks bot. Pushed doc PR: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/990 — includes CSV fix, model card limits update, migration blurb, and an example snippet showing legacy/new keys.

jin: running the SDK integration tests locally now...

alex: CI green on SDK side, but docs lint failed on link checker: the Optimize guide link we inserted is redirecting. I'll update link to canonical path.

natalie: fixed redirect, pushed force-update to PR 990. All checks passing except flakey bench in one region.

jin: awesome work. Next steps: merge SDK PR (alex), merge docs PR (natalie) and then create a short note in the release highlights for the week. I'll coordinate with growth for a quick banner for any users using Petra-Lite.

dan: add me to the release note so I can include the perf correction in the benchmarks page.

sara: thanks everyone :rocket:
